Trump Mobile appears to have suffered a data breach that may have exposed the data of 3,615 people, reports PCMag and Straight Arrow News.  

The breach reportedly included names, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, and order information.  PCMag and Straight Arrow News contacted several individuals in the dataset, who confirmed that the leaked information was accurate.  Some of the affected people never fully signed up for Trump Mobile; one individual told PCMag that they never managed to set up their account but still gave the company their email address and phone number.  

The full story is available at The Verge.
summary: Trump Mobile suffered a data breach that may have exposed the data of 3,615 people, including names, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, and order information. The leaked data also included information from people who never fully signed up for Trump Mobile, as confirmed by individuals contacted by PCMag and Straight Arrow News.
author: The Verge

title: Leaked Images Reveal Fitbit Edge Price and Features
content:
New leaks have shed additional light on Google’s upcoming Fitbit Edge fitness tracker, including pricing and key specifications. Images of the device were shared by Android Headlines, and further details were released a few days later.

According to leaked information from Dealabs, the Fitbit Edge will retail for €179 in Europe and £159 in the United Kingdom. 9to5Google estimates that the device will cost around $180 in the United States, based on the €99/£85 pricing of the $99 screen‑free Fitbit Air in those regions.

The tracker will feature a 1.34‑inch always‑on OLED touchscreen, run Fitbit OS with access to Google Play, and connect to Android and iOS devices over Blue… The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: Leaked images show the Google Fitbit Edge will sell for €179 in Europe and £159 in the UK, with an estimated US price of $180. The device will feature a 1.34‑inch always‑on OLED touchscreen, run Fitbit OS, and connect to Android and iOS devices via Bluetooth.
author: The Verge

title: Arturia Adds Sound Edit Menu to AstroLab 2.0 Firmware
content:
Arturia has released a firmware update for its AstroLab series that expands the keyboards’ capabilities beyond preset browsing. The new AstroLab 2.0 update introduces a Sound Edit menu, allowing users to access and adjust the individual parameters of any instrument.

Prior to the update, the AstroLab series—already regarded as one of the best stage keyboards—offered the AnalogLab suite of vintage synth emulations, sampled pianos, and original instrument plugins in a hardware format. However, it was limited to lightly tweaking patches with four macro controls and dialing in effects, providing no real sound‑design functionality.

With the addition of the Sound Edit menu, the AstroLab 2.0 firmware lets musicians dig into each instrument’s parameters, enabling genuine sound design directly on the hardware.
summary: Arturia's AstroLab series, previously limited to preset browsing, now includes a Sound Edit menu in the AstroLab 2.0 firmware that allows users to adjust individual instrument parameters. The update enables deeper sound design beyond the four macro controls and preset adjustments.
author: The Verge

title: HBO Max and Paramount Plus to merge into single streamer under Skydance
content:
HBO Max and Paramount Plus are set to merge into a single streaming service under the brand Skydance, following Paramount’s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The consolidation was announced in a press release that marked the completion of the deal.

Skydance, the name of the combined companies, stated that the two streamers will “unify into a single service over time.” Skydance CEO David Ellison previously suggested the merger could bring the combined platforms “a little over 200 million direct‑to‑consumer subscribers,” according to a March call with investors.

No details have yet been released regarding the timing of the merger or the eventual name of the merged service.
summary: HBO Max and Paramount Plus will merge into a single streaming service under Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, with the combined companies named Skydance. Skydance CEO David Ellison said the merger would bring a little over 200 million direct‑to‑consumer subscribers, though no timing or final name has been announced.
author: The Verge

title: Big Oil asks Supreme Court to halt climate lawsuits over state deception claims
content:
Oil companies have petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court to dismiss climate lawsuits before they reach trial, arguing that federal law should bar state claims of climate deception.  

The companies contend that the alleged deceptive practices by states should be prevented under existing federal statutes.
summary: Oil companies have asked the Supreme Court to dismiss climate lawsuits before trial. They say federal law should block state climate deception claims.
author: Ars Technica

title: Mistral AI releases new Mistral Large 4 multimodal model to surpass US and China rivals
content:
French AI lab Mistral AI has released a new large multimodal model, referred to in the title as a 1T model and named Mistral Large 4 in the source. The release is positioned as a step to leapfrog its competitors.  

The model is described as aiming to surpass both American and Chinese rivals, while the title highlights its intent to leapfrog closed and open rivals.  

No additional details are provided.
summary: French AI lab Mistral AI released the Mistral Large 4 model. It is a large multimodal model that aims to leapfrog American and Chinese rivals.
author: TechCrunch

title: Vinod Khosla says ex-DeepMind engineer’s Wajo will win agent market on trust
content:
Vinod Khosla has expressed confidence that Wajo, a startup founded by an ex‑DeepMind engineer, will dominate the agent market by building trust.  

Wajo’s flagship product, the Fo agent, is designed to outsource tasks to human workers, enabling it to handle complex requests that require human judgment.  

Khosla’s endorsement highlights the company’s focus on combining advanced technology with reliable human support to secure a competitive edge in the rapidly growing agent market.
summary: Vinod Khosla believes the ex‑DeepMind engineer’s company Wajo will win the agent market on trust. Wajo’s Fo agent can hire humans to complete a task.
author: TechCrunch

title: LibreOffice declares “no AI” a software feature, citing privacy concerns
content:
LibreOffice announced that “no AI” is now a software feature, confirming the open‑source document editor will not incorporate artificial‑intelligence functions in its default configuration.  

The organization said it has no plans to add AI to the core product, citing concerns over user privacy as the primary reason for the decision.
summary: LibreOffice says it will not add AI to the default configuration of its open source document editor. The decision is based on concerns about user privacy.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic offers startups free year of Claude Team and $1,000 credits
content:
Anthropic announced a program that provides startups with a free year of access to its Claude Team AI platform along with $1,000 in usage credits.  

The company said the initiative is intended to help emerging firms build products on top of its models, noting, “We created this program because we believe the benefits of AI will reach most people through the companies that build on top of models, rather than through the models alone.”  

The offer aims to support startups in developing AI‑driven solutions by removing cost barriers for a full year of Claude Team services.
summary: Anthropic created a program that gives startups a free year of Claude Team access and $1,000 in credits. The company said the program aims to spread AI benefits through companies that build on its models.
author: TechCrunch

title: Drax datacentre could emit nearly twice the yearly emissions of all Gatwick flights
content:
A campaign group’s analysis of Drax’s proposed data centre in North Yorkshire says the facility would need to burn 4.9 million tonnes of wood each year. The group estimates that the resulting emissions would be almost twice the total emissions generated by all flights departing from Gatwick Airport annually.

The analysis characterises the planned data centre as “one of the dirtiest datacentres out there,” highlighting the scale of wood consumption required to power the operation. The findings raise concerns about the environmental impact of the project.
summary: A campaign group’s analysis of Drax’s North Yorkshire datacentre plans says it would have to burn 4.9m tonnes of wood each year. The analysis finds the facility could produce nearly double the emissions of all flights out of Gatwick airport each year, which campaigners describe as one of the dirtiest datacentres.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI‑created meme character Triple T sparks international legal battle over copyright
content:
A legal dispute over the ownership of the internet meme “Tung Tung Tung Sahur” has escalated into an international battle that could shape the boundary between human creativity and artificial intelligence.  

The character, also known as Triple T, was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teenager who uses the online handle Noxa, employing OpenAI’s image‑generation tool. Modeled after a kentongan—a drum used to wake Southeast Asian Muslims for the pre‑dawn Ramadan meal—the anthropomorphized figure features a broad smile and a vacant stare and appears in videos classified under the “Italian brain rot” genre.  

U.S. copyright law, which protects only human‑made works, is being tested by the case, as the AI‑generated nature of Triple T raises questions about legal ownership and the applicability of existing intellectual‑property rules. The outcome may determine how courts treat AI‑created characters in the future.
summary: The AI‑generated character Tung Tung Tung Sahur, also called Triple T, was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teen using OpenAI’s image‑generation tool. The meme’s popularity has led to an international legal dispute over whether U.S. copyright law, which applies only to human‑made works, can cover the character.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Survey finds AI misuse tops brand reputational threats
content:
A new edition of the quarterly Reputation Risk Index released on Tuesday found that misusing artificial intelligence (AI) is the top reputational threat facing companies, according to a survey of more than 150 public‑affairs leaders. The respondents ranked AI misuse above concerns such as accusations of endangering children’s mental, emotional or physical well‑being and issues linked to the US‑Israel war on Iran, among other brand risks.

The survey results were highlighted in the latest Reputation Risk Index, which tracks emerging threats to corporate reputation. The findings come amid warnings from leading technology figures that AI placed in the wrong hands could precipitate larger existential dangers, including the possibility of nuclear conflict or bioweapon devastation.
summary: A new survey of more than 150 public affairs leaders found that misusing artificial intelligence is the top reputational threat for companies, ahead of risks such as child safety concerns and issues linked to the US‑Israel war on Iran. The findings were released in the latest quarterly Reputation Risk Index on Tuesday.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Ofcom probes Meta over safety checks for Instagram Instants feature
content:
Ofcom is investigating Meta over the safety of its Instagram Instants feature, a Snapchat‑style addition to the platform. The communications regulator is assessing whether the $1.9 trillion (£1.4 trillion) company complied with the UK Online Safety Act’s requirement for a risk assessment of illegal content and child access.

The probe focuses on whether Meta failed to conduct adequate checks on Instagram Instants to ensure it does not display illegal material or become accessible to children, which could constitute a breach of the Online Safety Act. Ofcom’s inquiry is ongoing.
summary: Ofcom is investigating Meta over its Instagram Instants feature to determine if the company complied with the Online Safety Act. The probe focuses on whether Meta performed adequate risk assessments to prevent illegal content and child access on the Snapchat‑style product.
author: Guardian Technology

title: ASOS app users get push notifications that appear to be from hackers
content: Dozens of users of the ASOS clothing and beauty store’s mobile app reported receiving a push notification that was described as a “strange message.” The notification appears to have been sent by hackers, according to the report. No additional details about the content of the message or any response from ASOS have been provided.
summary: Dozens of people received a strange push notification from the ASOS app. The message seemed to have been sent by hackers.
author: BBC Technology

title: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni files to trademark voice against AI deepfakes
content: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has filed a four‑second audio clip with a European Union agency to protect her voice from deepfake manipulation. The submission is part of an effort to trademark her voice and prevent its unauthorized use in AI‑generated content.
summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni filed a request to trademark her voice. She submitted a four‑second audio clip to an EU agency to protect it from deepfake misuse.
author: BBC Technology

title: Mermaid Polska Deepspot Cup turns mermaiding into sport in Warsaw's deepest pool
content:
Mermaids compete in Warsaw's deepest swimming pool

The Warsaw Mermaid Polska Deepspot Cup has transformed mermaiding into a competitive sport and artistic performance. Participants showcase acrobatics and take part in races, drawing increasing attention from women and children. The event highlights the growing popularity of mermaiding in the city.
summary: The Mermaid Polska Deepspot Cup in Warsaw features mermaids competing in the city's deepest swimming pool. The event includes acrobatics and races and is gaining popularity among women and children.
author: Euronews

title: Latest news bulletin: Oct 6, 2026 – Midday – Europe and beyond stories
content:
A news bulletin titled “Latest news bulletin | October 6th, 2026 – Midday” was released, inviting readers to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond on that date.

The bulletin highlights coverage of the day’s latest and breaking news across a range of topics, including world affairs, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
summary: The bulletin provides the most important stories from Europe and beyond on October 6, 2026. It covers breaking news in World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, and Travel.
author: Euronews

title: Qatar warns global costs of Iran war as mediation talks continue
content:
Qatar warned that “the whole world is paying” for the war in Iran, saying the conflict has disrupted global trade and prompted regional powers to strengthen Saudi Arabia’s defences.

Doha confirmed that diplomatic talks aimed at ending the war remain active and expressed support for the Mecca defence alliance, though it said it is still too early to discuss Qatar’s own membership in the pact.
summary: The Iran war has disrupted global trade while regional powers prepare to strengthen Saudi Arabia’s defences. Qatar said talks to end the war remained active, it backs the Mecca defence alliance, but it is too early to discuss joining the pact.
author: Euronews

title: Russia says Darya Shipilova died of unknown pneumonia, quarantines colleagues
content:
Rospotrebnadzor has denied that the death of a 28‑year‑old worker at the Irkutsk Anti‑Plague Institute was caused by plague, citing pneumonia of unknown aetiology. The agency stated that there were no links between the illness and the employee’s work at the institute.

Despite the denial, the ministry imposed quarantine on the deceased’s contacts, confined 60 colleagues inside the facility, and restricted access to hospitals, including a maternity ward. No further explanation was provided for the broad containment measures.
summary: Rospotrebnadzor said 28‑year‑old Darya Shipilova died of pneumonia of unknown aetiology with no link to her work at the Irkutsk Anti‑Plague Institute. Authorities quarantined her contacts, confined 60 colleagues inside the institute and limited access to nearby hospitals, including a maternity ward.
author: Euronews

title: 15‑year‑old student kills one, wounds eight in Istanbul school stabbing
content:
A stabbing attack at Şeyh Şamil Imam Hatip Secondary School in the Başakşehir district of Istanbul left one student dead and eight others wounded on Tuesday morning.  

Police say the assailant was a 15‑year‑old student who entered the school disguised in the institution’s uniform before targeting pupils.  

The suspect, who attends a different school, was taken into custody shortly after the incident.
summary: A 15‑year‑old student disguised in the target school's uniform attacked pupils at Şeyh Şamil Imam Hatip Secondary School in Başakşehir on Tuesday morning, killing one student and wounding eight. The suspect, who attends a different school, was apprehended.
author: Euronews

title: Tens of thousands march across France supporting student education funding protests
content:
Tens of thousands of demonstrators marched in cities across France on Tuesday in support of school pupils demanding increased education funding.  

The rally, which drew teachers and trade unions, added pressure on the government of outgoing President Emmanuel Macron. According to France 24’s Marc Perelman, the students aim to turn the protests into a “major social movement” to heighten that pressure.
summary: Tens of thousands of demonstrators marched in cities across France on Tuesday in support of school pupils demanding more education funding. Teachers and trade unions joined the march as students aim to turn the protests into a major social movement to increase pressure on the government of outgoing President Emmanuel Macron, according to France 24's Marc Perelman.
author: France 24

title: Ex-hostage Shoshan Haran says Israelis were naive about Hamas before Oct 7 attack
content:
In an interview with FRANCE 24, former Israeli hostage Shoshan Haran said “we were naive” about Hamas before the October 7, 2023 attack on her kibbutz.  

Haran recounted that she was held in Gaza for 50 days and that she refused to “show weakness” to her captors during that period. She also described accusations of genocide against Israel as “a lie” and shared the last words of her late husband.  

The remarks were made by Haran during the televised interview.
summary: In an interview with France 24, Israeli former hostage Shoshan Haran said she and others were naive about Hamas before the October 7, 2023 attack on her kibbutz. She recalled spending 50 days held in Gaza, refusing to show weakness to her captors, called accusations of genocide against Israel a lie, and shared her late husband's last words.
author: France 24

title: Kenya records first Ebola death as returnee from DR Congo dies
content:
Kenya reported its first Ebola death on Tuesday after a Kenyan national who had been residing in the Democratic Republic of Congo died following his return to Kenya.  

The fatality makes Kenya the fourth country to record an Ebola case in the ongoing outbreak that was declared in eastern DR Congo in mid‑May.
summary: Kenya reported its first Ebola death after a Kenyan national who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo died upon returning. Kenya is the fourth country to record an Ebola case in the current outbreak that began in eastern DR Congo in mid‑May.
author: France 24

title: Paris Fashion Week front row dazzles with Nicole Kidman, Dua Lipa, Rihanna
content:
Paris Fashion Week returned to the city this season with the spring‑summer 2027 collections dominating the runways. Front‑row seats were occupied by high‑profile guests including Nicole Kidman, Dua Lipa and Rihanna, drawing additional attention to the shows.

Simon Moritz highlighted several marquee presentations, beginning with Matthieu Blazy’s tribute to the women who shaped Gabrielle Chanel, which unfolded at the historic Chanel house. The coverage also noted notable shifts at YSL, Balenciaga and Dior, and introduced Lithuanian designer Juozas Statkevicius, who showcased pieces inspired by his national heritage.
summary: Paris Fashion Week featured the spring‑summer 2027 collections with Nicole Kidman, Dua Lipa and Rihanna lighting up the front row. The shows highlighted Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel presentation and collections from YSL, Balenciaga, Dior and Lithuanian designer Juozas Statkevicius.
author: France 24

title: Moscow says Ukraine launched nearly 900 drones across Russia overnight
content:
Russian air defenses intercepted nearly 900 Ukrainian drones overnight across multiple regions of Russia, the occupied Crimean Peninsula and the Sea of Azov, the Defense Ministry in Moscow said on Tuesday. The ministry’s statement described the large-scale drone activity as one of the biggest Ukrainian strikes on Russian territory since the war began.

France 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg noted that, if the figures are accurate, the attack would rank among the largest drone assaults launched by Ukraine against Russia to date. The Defense Ministry provided the numbers in its Tuesday report.
summary: Russian air defenses intercepted nearly 900 Ukrainian drones overnight over multiple regions of Russia, the occupied Crimean Peninsula and the Sea of Azov, the Defense Ministry in Moscow said Tuesday. If the figures are accurate, it would be one of the largest Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia since the start of the war, said France 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg.
author: France 24

title: Tens of thousands protest French schools as police fire tear gas
content:
Police deployed tear‑gas on Tuesday as demonstrators blockaded French high schools, part of the largest day of action in a wave of protests over understaffed and dilapidated classrooms. Tens of thousands of students, teachers and parents took to the streets nationwide.

In Paris, the march remained peaceful according to France 24 reporter Claire Paccalin, who described the atmosphere as “tense” amid a “heavy police presence.” The demonstrations reflect growing frustration with the condition of school facilities across the country.
summary: Police fired tear gas at protesters blockading French high schools on Tuesday as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of action in a wave of demonstrations against understaffed and dilapidated classrooms. In Paris, the march reported by France 24’s Claire Paccalin remained peaceful but tense with a heavy police presence.
author: France 24

title: Norway proposes temporary ban on smart glasses in public places
content:
Norway's government announced on Monday that it intends to introduce a temporary ban on the use of smart glasses in a range of public venues, citing privacy concerns over covert image recording.

The proposed restriction could apply to parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres, schools, daycare centres, healthcare facilities, gyms and public events.
summary: Norway's government said Monday it wants a temporary ban on the use of smart glasses in certain public places, citing privacy concerns about recording images without people's knowledge. The ban could apply to parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres, schools, daycare centres, healthcare facilities, gyms and public events.
author: France 24

title: Tens of thousands protest across France demanding better education conditions
content:
Tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday, demanding better education. The large crowds reflected a growing call for improved learning conditions.

Unions and teachers joined high‑school students who have been protesting for days, and the demonstrations have been punctuated by violent confrontations.
summary: Tens of thousands of demonstrators marched across France on Tuesday, joined by unions, teachers and high‑school students. The protests have been ongoing for days, with participants demanding better learning conditions and some confrontations turning violent.
author: France 24

title: Fact check: Russian plague lab claims of accident and spread are misleading
content:
A laboratory worker died at a plague research institute in Russia, prompting a wave of claims that a lab accident had occurred, that hundreds of people were infected, and that the disease had spread internationally.  

Fact‑checking organizations have found that many of these narratives are misleading. The reports of a large‑scale outbreak and cross‑border transmission are not supported by the available evidence.
summary: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has led to claims of a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Those viral narratives are misleading.
author: DW World

title: Abiy Ahmed faces regional alliance as Tigray war risks spilling into Eritrea
content:
The Tigray war may spread into neighboring Eritrea, a risk analysts link to rhetoric from Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.  

Abiy Ahmed is consolidating power domestically while confronting a regional alliance that opposes him.  The ongoing conflict in Tigray is seen as having the potential to spill over across the border into Eritrea.  

The development highlights the broader challenges facing Abiy as he balances internal consolidation with mounting regional tensions.
summary: Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is consolidating power. He must contend with a regional alliance opposing him and a Tigray conflict that could spill over into Eritrea.
author: DW World

title: Iran hardliners shift from street morality police to workplace pressure on hijab compliance
content:
More Iranian women are increasingly refusing to comply with the state‑mandated hijab rules, prompting a shift in how authorities seek to enforce the dress code.  

Hardline officials are moving away from reliance on the “morality police” to police the streets and are instead applying social pressure within workplaces, service sectors and businesses to compel adherence.
summary: More women in Iran are rejecting the rules requiring them to wear hijab headscarves. Hardliners are moving from street enforcement by the morality police to applying social pressure in workplaces, services and businesses.
author: DW World

title: Paramount completes $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, forming new entertainment giant
content:
Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, forming a new entertainment behemoth under the ownership of Skydance.  

The deal was driven by billionaire David Ellison’s hostile takeover bid, which overcame competing efforts from Netflix.  

The merger creates a single Hollywood giant that combines Paramount’s and Warner Bros. Discovery’s assets and operations.
summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery. The deal, led by billionaire David Ellison’s Skydance, defeated a rival Netflix bid.
author: DW World

title: Intense fighting in Yemen displaces over 184,000 people, IOM says
content: Intense fighting in Yemen has displaced more than 184,000 people from their homes, the United Nations migration agency (IOM) reported on Monday. The agency said the displacement began at the start of August, with the majority of those forced to flee occurring since early September.
summary: Intense fighting in Yemen has forced more than 184,000 people from their homes since the start of August. Most of them were displaced since early September, the UN migration agency (IOM) said on Monday.
author: UN News

title: UN Rights Chief Volker Türk warns AI regulation deadline looming
content:
UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk warned Monday that the world is running out of time to put guardrails on artificial intelligence.  

Türk said the “ruthless race” between companies and countries raises concerns about human safety and even humanity’s survival.
summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said the world is running out of time to put guardrails on artificial intelligence. He warned that a ruthless race between companies and countries raises concerns for human safety and humanity’s survival.
author: UN News

title: UN chief Guterres says nothing can justify 7 October atrocities, three years later
content:
UN Secretary‑General António Guterres said that “nothing can justify these atrocities” on the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks carried out by Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups against Israel.  

He called for an end to the suffering of both Israelis and Palestinians, emphasizing the need to halt the violence and its humanitarian impact.
summary: Three years after Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups attacked Israel, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said nothing can justify the atrocities of 7 October. He called for an end to the suffering of Israelis and Palestinians alike.
author: UN News

title: Central Africa Seizes Over 250 Tonnes of Illicit Medical Products in Six Years
content:
When streets become pharmacies, illicit markets in Central Africa are growing rapidly. The region’s fragile health systems create conditions that allow these markets to thrive.

Over six years, authorities seized more than 250 tonnes of medical products, including antibiotics, malaria treatments, painkillers, and opioids. The seizure volume underscores the scale of the underground trade.

The market’s success is not merely a consequence of weak health infrastructure; it also benefits from it, allowing illicit distributors to operate with relative ease.
summary: More than 250 tonnes of antibiotics, malaria treatments, painkillers, and opioids were seized in Central Africa over six years. The illicit market thrives partly because of the region’s fragile health systems.
author: UN News

title: UNICEF says Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC robs children of loved ones
content:
UNICEF warned that the Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is depriving children of the people they depend on.  

The agency said the disease is also claiming the lives of some children themselves, according to a report released on Tuesday.
summary: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is robbing children of their loved ones. UNICEF reported on Tuesday that some children have also died from the disease.
author: UN News

title: UN Secretary-General calls for end to US-Iran conflict during Pakistan visit
content:
The United Nations Secretary‑General António Guterres called for an end to the United States‑Iran conflict during an official visit to Pakistan. He made the appeal on Tuesday, urging that the war be halted.

Guterres highlighted the toll the conflict has taken on global trade, stressing the need for a swift resolution to mitigate economic disruptions.
summary: The UN Secretary-General appealed on Tuesday for an end to the United States-Iran war. He began an official visit to Pakistan, citing the war's toll on global trade.
author: UN News

title: Argentina says it will halt Falklands offshore oil exploitation, foreign minister declares
content:
Argentina’s foreign minister, Pablo Quirno, announced that the Argentine government will halt the Falkland Islands’ exploitation of offshore oilfields. Quirno said the move is part of a broader strategy to peacefully assert Argentine sovereignty over the islands.

The statement was made during a speech at a think‑tank event in the Argentine capital, where Quirno addressed an audience that included the British ambassador. He condemned the British government for failing to open negotiations over the islands and for facilitating a significant offshore oil project in the surrounding waters.
summary: Argentina’s foreign minister Pablo Quirno announced that his government will stop the Falkland Islands from exploiting offshore oilfields. He said the action is part of a strategy to peacefully assert sovereignty and condemned the British government for not opening negotiations and facilitating the oil project.
author: Guardian World

title: Survivors in Gaza Say Recovery From Trauma Is Impossible
content:
In Gaza, survivors say that recovery is not on the horizon. They describe the situation as one where the trauma of recent events has left them unable to begin healing.

According to the statement, the genocide has killed many and left the rest broken. The survivors emphasize that the damage inflicted has made any prospect of recovery seem distant.

The statement reflects the ongoing suffering of those who have survived the conflict.
summary: The genocide in Gaza has killed many and left survivors broken. Survivors say recovery is not on the horizon.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel faces deadline to close UK consulate as Sir Vincent Fean calls actions unlawful
content:
Israel’s deadline to close the United Kingdom’s consulate is drawing near, prompting diplomatic tension.  

Former British consul Sir Vincent Fean said the Israeli government is acting unlawfully in the wake of a new wave of sanctions, describing the move as “not the act of a friend.”
summary: Israel's deadline to close the UK consulate is approaching. Former British consul Sir Vincent Fean says Israel is acting unlawfully after a new wave of sanctions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bulgaria searches for missing crew after drones sink Togo‑flagged Alfa Watan in Black Sea
content: Bulgaria has launched a search operation for the missing crew of two vessels that were struck by drones in the Black Sea. The Togo‑flagged ship Alfa Watan sank at the scene of the attack, prompting authorities to begin the rescue effort. The incident involved drones hitting both ships, leading to the loss of the Alfa Watan and the disappearance of crew members. Bulgarian officials are conducting the search to locate the missing personnel.
summary: Bulgaria has launched a search operation for the missing crew of two ships hit by drones in the Black Sea. The Togo‑flagged vessel Alfa Watan sank at the scene of the attack.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Croatia vs Spain UEFA Nations League live coverage led by Lamine Yamal
content: A live text commentary stream is covering the UEFA Nations League match between Croatia and Spain. The coverage provides real‑time updates, build‑up information and team news, with Lamine Yamal highlighted as the headline feature. The stream offers fans continuous details as the game unfolds.
summary: The match between Croatia and Spain in the UEFA Nations League is being covered live with text commentary. Lamine Yamal is highlighted in the coverage.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Norway files three complaints urging FIFA Ethics Committee to review Infantino's conduct
content:
Norway’s football governing body has lodged three formal complaints with FIFA’s Ethics Committee, challenging the conduct of FIFA chief Gianni Infantino and alleging an “abuse of power.”  

The complaints request that the Ethics Committee examine Infantino’s actions, prompting a formal inquiry into the allegations raised by the Norwegian federation.
summary: Norway's football body submitted three complaints. The complaints ask FIFA's Ethics Committee to examine Infantino's conduct.
author: Al Jazeera

title: AfD candidate Tobias Rausch elected speaker of German regional parliament for first time
content:
Tobias Rausch, running for the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), was elected speaker of a German regional parliament, the first time the party has secured that post.  

Although the speaker’s duties are largely symbolic, opponents have described the outcome as a watershed moment.
summary: Tobias Rausch, an AfD candidate, was elected speaker of a German regional parliament. Opponents said the largely symbolic role marks a watershed moment.
author: BBC World

title: Belgian physicist Francis Halzen wins physics Nobel for space particle observatory
content:
Belgian physicist Prof Francis Halzen has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his pioneering work on an observatory that detects particles from space. The prize recognizes his contributions to the study of “ghost particles,” which are observed using a space‑based telescope.

Halzen’s observatory enables the detection of these high‑energy particles originating beyond Earth, marking a significant advancement in astrophysical research. The Nobel Committee highlighted his role in developing the instrument that makes such observations possible.
summary: Belgian physicist Prof Francis Halzen has won the physics Nobel. He was recognized for his pioneering work on an observatory that detects particles from space.
author: BBC World

title: Cornell 7 lawyer urges removal of AG Letitia James over prior comments
content:
A lawyer representing one of the Cornell 7 has urged that the special prosecutor be removed, citing the prosecutor’s prior remarks about the case.

New York Attorney General Letitia James is conducting the investigation into the rape allegations, but the lawyer argues that comments James made on the matter should disqualify her from serving as special prosecutor.
summary: A lawyer for a member of the Cornell 7 has called for New York Attorney General Letitia James to be removed as special prosecutor. The lawyer says James’s comments on the rape allegations should disqualify her.
author: BBC World

title: White House defends Trump's comment about letting Iran target Los Angeles and San Diego
content:
The White House defended a recent comment by former President Donald Trump in which he suggested Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego, saying the remark was intended as a warning about the danger of a nuclear‑armed Iran.  

California Governor Gavin Newsom described Trump’s remarks as “deranged,” while the White House insisted the former president was merely highlighting the risk posed by a nuclear‑capable Iran.
summary: Gavin Newsom called the remarks “deranged”. The White House said Trump was warning of the risk of a nuclear Iran.
author: BBC World

title: Ship sinks after Black Sea drone attack, crew missing
content:
A ship sank in the Black Sea after a drone attack, leaving its crew missing.  

The source of the drone strike has not been identified, and officials have not confirmed who carried out the attack. The incident occurs amid a period in which Russia has stepped up strikes across the Black Sea as part of its ongoing war against Ukraine.
summary: A ship sank after a drone attack in the Black Sea, and its crew are missing. It is not clear who is behind the attacks which come as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea as part of its war against Ukraine.
author: BBC World

title: Former German spy chief August Hanning arrested on espionage and treason charges
content: Former German intelligence chief August Hanning has been arrested on charges of espionage and treason. Authorities say Hanning, who previously led Germany’s spy agency, is accused of obtaining classified information for a foreign power. The arrest follows allegations that he transferred sensitive data to an external entity. No further details about the investigation have been released.
summary: August Hanning, a former German spy chief, was arrested on espionage and treason charges. He is accused of obtaining classified information for a foreign power.
author: BBC World

title: Falcons beat Saints 45-24, souring Domecoming 20th‑anniversary celebrations
content:
The Atlanta Falcons defeated the New Orleans Saints 45‑24 on Monday night, ending a day of festivities that had been meant to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Superdome’s reopening after Hurricane Katrina.

Three plays into the game, Falcons running back Bijan Robinson scored a 59‑yard touchdown that silenced the electric Superdome crowd. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough described his performance as “embarrassed,” while second‑year head coach Kellen Moore said he was “disappointed” and “frustrated” with the team’s showing.

The loss stood in stark contrast to the Saints’ landmark 23‑3 victory over the Falcons 20 years earlier, when Steve Gleason blocked a punt and Curtis Deloatch recovered it for a touchdown, a moment that had become a symbol of the franchise’s triumph after the hurricane‑damaged stadium was reopened.
summary: The Atlanta Falcons defeated the New Orleans Saints 45-24, with Bijan Robinson scoring a 59‑yard touchdown run three plays into the game and silencing the Superdome crowd. The loss dampened festivities marking the 20th anniversary of the Saints’ return to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jason McCarthy retires at 29 to coach Brighton U21s
content:
Jason McCarthy, a former Wycombe defender, has retired from professional football at the age of 29 to pursue a career in coaching. McCarthy, who considered becoming a pastor before staying in the game, began his coaching journey by leading Wycombe’s foundation under-16s while still an active player. He recently returned to his position as Brighton’s under-21s assistant coach after serving as interim head coach for two months this summer.

During his interim period, McCarthy stepped in while head coach Shannon Ruth supported Fabian Hürzeler’s first-team staff. McCarthy expressed strong admiration for Hürzeler, the 33-year-old Brighton head coach who became the youngest permanent manager in Premier League history at age 31. Hürzeler was also part of McCarthy’s interview process for his current role.
summary: Jason McCarthy retired from football at age 29 after serving as a defender for Wycombe, having previously coached the club's under-16s. He currently serves as Brighton's under-21s assistant coach and recently returned to that role after two months in interim charge.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Coco Gauff Receives Racist Abuse After Disputed Point at China Open
content:
Coco Gauff reported receiving an “insane” volume of racist comments on social media following a disputed point during her China Open match against Sun Xinran. The American player stopped a rally late in the first set after electronic advertising boards lining the court flickered, which distracted her during the point.

Gauff went on to win the third-round match 7-5, 6-1. Her opponent, Sun Xinran, is a 16-year-old home player who recently won the US Open junior title.
summary: Coco Gauff said she received an “insane” amount of racist comments on social media after a controversial point in her China Open match. She stopped a rally when electronic advertising boards flickered during a point late in the first set of her 7-5, 6-1 third‑round victory over Sun Xinran, a 16‑year‑old US Open junior champion.
author: Guardian Sport

title: David Squires cartoon marks 25 years of Beckham's England v Greece heroics
content:
Cartoonist David Squires has marked the 25th anniversary of David Beckham’s performance for England against Greece with a new cartoon. The artwork depicts the England midfielder’s "one-man rescue act" at Old Trafford.

Squires has also promoted his latest book, Chaos in the Box, alongside the new illustration.
summary: Cartoonist David Squires reflects on the 25th anniversary of David Beckham's one-man rescue act for England against Greece. The piece highlights the match at Old Trafford and promotes Squires' latest book, Chaos in the Box.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Messi's Argentina career ends in friendly vs Benin
content:
Lionel Messi’s international career with Argentina is set to conclude in a friendly match against Benin. The 39‑year‑old will play his final game for the national team before stepping away from international football.

BBC Sport is examining what lies ahead for Messi following the end of this golden era. The coverage will focus on his next moves after retiring from the Argentine side.
summary: Lionel Messi's final appearance for Argentina will be in a friendly against Benin. BBC Sport examines what the 39‑year‑old's future might hold.
author: BBC Sport

title: Lee Gi-hyuk apologises for gloating over military exemption after Asian Games gold
content: Lee Gi‑hyuk, the captain of South Korea’s football team, issued an apology after it was reported that he had gloating about avoiding the country’s mandatory military service. The apology came in the wake of his remarks praising his role in leading South Korea to a gold medal at the Asian Games.
summary: Lee Gi-hyuk apologises for gloating about avoiding South Korea's mandatory military service. He captained his country to a football gold medal at the Asian Games.
author: BBC Sport

title: LIV Golf Secures Possible $300M Financing from BC Partners Credit
content: LIV Golf has secured a potential $300 million financing arrangement from BC Partners Credit. The funding is intended to help the organization emerge from its current restructuring process. The goal is to be fully operational and financially stable before the 2027 season.
summary: LIV Golf secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit. The funding is intended to help the organization emerge from restructuring before the 2027 season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Sen. Tillis Calls Trump Jan. 6 Impeachment 'Weighty' Vote of No Confidence
content:
Sen. Thom Tillis (R‑N.C.) said on Monday that President Trump’s impeachment related to the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol Hill attack was “weighty” and that the impeachment trial was a “vote of no confidence.”  

Tillis made the remarks during an interview with MS NOW’s Ari Melber on “The Beat.”  The conversation also covered Tillis’s upcoming book, titled “How to Lose Friends and ….”
summary: Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) said President Trump's impeachment over the Jan. 6, 2021 Capitol Hill attack was weighty and a vote of no confidence. He spoke with MS NOW’s Ari Melber on “The Beat” about the impeachment and his upcoming book “How to Lose Friends and…”.
author: The Hill

title: Democrats hold major advantage on health care costs in new poll
content:
A new poll from health‑research group KFF found that health care costs remain a top affordability concern for voters. Six in 10 respondents said they are worried about being able to afford their health care, including the cost of health insurance.

The poll also revealed that voters trust Democrats more than Republicans on the issue of health care costs. According to the survey, the trust margin is nearly two‑to‑one in favor of Democrats.
summary: Health care costs are a top affordability concern for voters, according to a new poll by KFF. Voters trust Democrats over Republicans on the issue by a nearly two-to-one margin, with six in ten worried about affording health care.
author: The Hill

title: Musk, Luckey new Pentagon roles raise ethics worries
content:
Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey have recently taken on new roles within the Pentagon, a move that has sparked ethical concerns among observers.

According to a study on future autonomous weapon systems, Musk’s company SpaceX and Luckey’s company Anduril could potentially benefit from the recommendations outlined in the research.

The possibility that these companies stand to gain from the study’s findings has intensified scrutiny of the officials’ new positions.
summary: Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey have new roles in the Pentagon that raise ethics concerns. Their companies, SpaceX and Anduril, could benefit from recommendations on future autonomous weapon systems.
author: NPR Politics

title: Democrats' advantage clear with less than a month to midterm elections
content:
With less than a month remaining in the midterm elections, Democrats are said to have a clear advantage.

President Trump is facing low approval ratings, and voters are blaming him for rising costs.

Republicans are likely to pay the price at the ballot box next month.
summary: President Trump is facing low approval ratings, and voters blame him for rising costs. Republicans are likely to pay the price at the ballot box next month.
author: NPR Politics

title: FBI Spy Hunting Squads Cut Staff Amid Trump Focus on Crime and Immigration
content:
FBI's spy‑hunting squads hit with deep cuts even as foreign espionage threats soar

The FBI’s spy‑hunting squads have received significant budget cuts. The reductions come as a consequence of President Trump and FBI Director Kash Patel’s focus on violent crime and immigration, leaving other priorities understaffed.
summary: The FBI's spy hunting squads received deep cuts. These cuts result from President Trump's and FBI Director Kash Patel's focus on violent crime and immigration, leaving other priorities understaffed.
author: NPR Politics

title: Chile Reaffirms Bid to Host High Seas Treaty HQ Amid Chinese Rivalry
content:
Chile has reaffirmed its bid to host the High Seas Treaty headquarters, intensifying the race to secure the location.  

Chile’s strong ocean protection record and concerns over a rival Chinese bid keep it in play, even as questions arise about the Kast government’s environmental policies.  

The post appeared first on Climate Home News.
summary: Chile’s strong ocean protection record keeps it in the running to host the High Seas Treaty headquarters. The bid is challenged by concerns over a rival Chinese offer and questions about the Kast government’s environmental policies.
author: Climate Home News

title: Pacific leaders say fossil‑fuel transition not open to renegotiation at Tuvalu pre‑COP
content:
International leaders have flown to the low‑lying atoll nation of Tuvalu as part of climate talks co‑hosted by Australia ahead of the COP31 conference. The visit is aimed at building momentum for a global transition away from fossil fuels.

Pacific island leaders have urged that this promised transition must not be left open to renegotiation. They gathered in Tuvalu to highlight the plight of the countries most at risk from the climate crisis.

About 50 dignitaries attended, including 14 national heads such as Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, a number of climate‑change ministers and heads of global agencies. The delegation’s presence is intended to bring attention to the urgent need for a firm commitment to phasing out fossil fuels.
summary: Pacific island leaders gathered in Tuvalu ahead of COP31 to urge that the promised global transition away from fossil fuels not be left open to renegotiation. About 50 dignitaries, including 14 national heads such as Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, climate ministers and heads of global agencies, attended the Australia‑co‑hosted talks.
author: Guardian Environment

title: US households pay 62% more for water than a decade ago, study finds
content:
US households are paying 62 % more for drinking water than they did a decade ago, a new study has found, outpacing inflation, grocery prices and household incomes. The study, co‑authored by a Food & Water Watch researcher, attributes the steep rise to for‑profit water corporations, federal cuts and the climate crisis, which the authors say are “supercharging water rate hikes.”  

Food & Water Watch, a Washington DC‑based non‑profit, analyzed 2025 billing data from the 500 largest community water systems in the United States. These systems serve about 155 million people, roughly 45 % of the country’s population. The analysis compared current rates with data from a similar Food & Water Watch survey conducted in 2015. The study does not include wastewater or storm water charges, which are often billed separately from drinking water service.
summary: A study by Food & Water Watch found that US households are paying 62% more for drinking water than a decade ago, outpacing inflation, grocery prices and
author: Guardian Environment

title: Three Scientists Awarded Nobel Prize for Light‑Controlled Brain Cell Research
content:
Scientists who worked out how to control brain cells with light have won this year’s Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.  

The award was given to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their research into light‑gated ion channels and optogenetics.  

The prize recognizes their contributions to the field of optogenetics.
summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel received this year's Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for their research into light‑gated ion channels and optogenetics. Their work allows scientists to control brain cells with light.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak exceeds 1,000 cases, largest in over 30 years
content:
Pennsylvania has surpassed 1,000 measles cases this year, state health officials said Monday, making it the largest state outbreak in more than three decades.

The figure marks the most significant measles outbreak in the state in over thirty years, according to officials.
summary: Pennsylvania has reported more than 1,000 measles cases this year. State health officials said it is the largest state outbreak in more than three decades.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cancer trial drug may work differently than believed, raising clinical research concerns
content: A new study led by the University of Sydney, in collaboration with Goethe University, Oxford University, and the Institute of Cancer Research, London, suggests that a cancer drug currently in clinical trials may have been tested based on an incorrect understanding of its mechanism. The research indicates that the foundational scientific premise for the drug’s entry into patient trials may have been flawed, raising concerns about the validity of the ongoing clinical investigations.
summary: A new study led by the University of Sydney suggests a cancer drug in clinical trials may have been tested based on an incorrect understanding of its mechanism. The research was conducted in collaboration with Goethe University, Oxford University, and the Institute of Cancer Research, London.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Carefree shoppers most likely to receive retail discounts, study finds
content:
A study conducted by Durham University Business School has identified how retailers target customers who are likely to spend more. The research highlights that shoppers who adopt a more carefree approach to spending are more frequently offered personalized discount codes.

According to the findings, retailers use this insight to tailor promotions to individuals who demonstrate a relaxed attitude toward purchasing. The personalized discount codes are designed to encourage further spending among these customers.

The study underscores the link between carefree spending habits and the likelihood of receiving targeted retail discounts.
summary: Research involving Durham University Business School shows retailers target customers likely to spend more. Carefree shoppers are more likely to receive personalized discount codes from retailers.
author: Phys.org

title: Russian worker at Siberian plague institute dies of unknown pneumonia
content:
Russian authorities have quarantined a hospital and are monitoring contacts after a worker at a plague research institute in Siberia contracted pneumonia of an “unknown” cause.  

The employee, a woman, reportedly died last week, according to local state TV.  

The quarantine and contact‑monitoring measures are being implemented by Russian authorities in response to the incident.
summary: Russian authorities quarantined a hospital and are monitoring contacts of an employee at a plague research institute in Siberia who contracted pneumonia of an unknown cause. Local state TV said the woman died last week.
author: Phys.org

title: Switching on brain cells: The Nobel-winning science of optogenetics
content:
Switching on brain cells: The Nobel‑winning science of optogenetics

Scientists are using light to control neurons in a technique called optogenetics. By stimulating brain cells with precise light signals, researchers can modulate neural activity in a highly targeted way.

This approach holds promise for developing new treatments for conditions such as dementia, depression and blindness.
summary: In optogenetics, scientists control neurons by stimulating them with light—potentially unlocking breakthroughs for conditions such as dementia, depression and blindness.
author: Phys.org

title: California scientist Karl Deisseroth wins Nobel Prize in medicine for optogenetics
content:
Dr. Karl Deisseroth received a Nobel Prize in Medicine early Monday after a long career in neuroscience. He spent hours fielding congratulatory calls from colleagues, friends, and the public following the announcement.  

The award recognizes his pioneering work in optogenetics, a field that uses light to control neurons and has opened new avenues for brain science.
summary: Dr. Karl Deisseroth spent hours fielding congratulatory calls after learning early Monday that he had won a Nobel Prize for medicine for helping to open a new field of brain science called optogenetics. He then made school lunches for his kids.
author: Phys.org

title: Global study finds ecosystems' ability to recover from species loss vastly overestimated
content:
A global analysis has found that the ability of ecosystems to recover after species loss has been vastly overestimated. The study, described as the largest of its kind, challenges the long‑held belief that nature carries ample backup, so that a small number of extinctions would cause little harm.

According to the analysis, ecosystems do not possess as much resilience as previously assumed. Even a modest loss of species can have significant negative impacts, contradicting the notion that nature can simply “bounce back” without consequence.
summary: The largest global study of its kind found that ecosystems' ability to bounce back after species loss is vastly overestimated. It says the idea that ecosystems have ample backup and suffer little harm when a small number of species go extinct is greatly overestimated.
author: Phys.org

title: FDA approves first drug that treats narcolepsy itself, not just symptoms
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the first drug that targets narcolepsy itself rather than only its symptoms, marking a potential shift for people living with the disorder.  

In a Guardian podcast, science reporter Madeleine Finlay discusses with editor Ian Sample how the scientific breakthrough that led to the approval unfolded.  

Julie Flygare, a person with narcolepsy who founded the non‑profit Project Sleep, describes the daily challenges of the condition and says the new medication could be a game‑changer for patients.
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved the first drug that treats narcolepsy itself rather than only its symptoms. In a Guardian podcast, Madeleine Finlay discusses the breakthrough with Ian Sample, and Julie Flygare, a narcolepsy patient and founder of Project Sleep, describes living with the condition and the drug’s potential impact.
author: Guardian Science

title: Seven early-onset cancers rise sharply in England, prostate cases quadruple since 2001
content:
International researchers examining data from the United Kingdom, United States and the Netherlands reported “significant increases” in early‑onset cases of seven cancers, prompting warnings that lifestyle choices are costing thousands of lives each year.

In England, the study found that diagnoses of seven cancer types among people under 50 have risen sharply. The number of under‑50 prostate cancer cases has quadrupled since 2001, while early‑onset bowel, kidney and uterine cancers have more than doubled.
summary: Experts analyzing UK, US and Dutch data identified significant increases in early‑onset cases of seven cancers among younger people in England. In England, diagnoses of prostate cancer in people under 50 have quadrupled since 2001, while early‑onset bowel, kidney and uterine cancers have more than doubled.
author: Guardian Science

title: Dissolved organic matter and suspended sediment mingle in Rupert Bay, southern James Bay
content: The Beaver Brown Waters of Rupert Bay have been observed to contain a mixture of dissolved organic matter and suspended sediment. This combination occurs in the southernmost extent of James Bay, where the two substances mingle within the water column.
summary: Dissolved organic matter and suspended sediment mingle in the southernmost extent of James Bay. This area is identified as Rupert Bay.

title: APOD October 6 2026 Features Complete Auroral Oval from SMILE
content:
The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) entry for 6 October 2026 is titled “A Complete Auroral Oval from SMILE.” The daily feature showcases an image of the auroral oval captured by the SMILE mission and includes a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

The APOD archive lists the submission under its standard categories, noting involvement from ESA and CAS among the contributors. The entry is part of the ongoing APOD series that presents a different astronomical image each day.
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day for October 6 2026 shows a complete auroral oval captured by SMILE. The entry includes a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

title: UK oil refinery exceeded toxic pollution limits dozens of times, documents show
content:
A UK oil refinery has breached toxic‑pollution limits dozens of times, documents reveal.  

The paperwork, obtained by the BBC, shows that pollution from the site was spilled into local rivers and protected areas.  

The documents were shared with the BBC.
summary: The documents reveal that a UK oil refinery broke toxic pollution limits dozens of times. Pollution was spilled into local rivers and protected sites, the documents shared with the BBC indicate.

A GitHub repository titled “firebird‑doom” showcases a version of the classic game DOOM that is simulated and rendered inside the Firebird SQL database using WebAssembly (WASM). The project is hosted at https://github.com/mariuz/firebird-doom.

content:
Amazon Prime Big Deal Days have launched, and a roundup of the top discounts is now available. The article, titled “80 Best Prime Day Deals We’re Shopping This October (2026),” lists eighty recommended deals on gear that the editorial team has selected.

The piece notes that the team has tracked down the best discounts offered during the Amazon Prime Big Deal Days, focusing on items they recommend. No additional specifics about the products, prices, or retailers are provided.

content:
An article titled “16 Best Prime Day Tech and Gadget Deals (October 2026)” presents a curated list of discounted technology and gadget offers for Prime Day. The piece emphasizes that shoppers can avoid paying full price by taking advantage of the featured deals.

content: Prime Day shoppers are already encountering discounts on Apple technology, according to a recent overview of the October 2026 sales event. The report notes that price reductions are appearing across a range of Apple devices as well as third‑party accessories.
summary: Discounts are already being offered on Apple devices. Third‑party accessories for Apple are also discounted.

title: 13 Amazon device deals worth buying on Prime Day
content:
Amazon is promoting 13 device deals for this year’s Prime Day, highlighting discounts that remain appealing despite recent price changes.  

The offers, while not as steep as they were before the August price hike, are still considered worthwhile for shoppers seeking Amazon hardware.
summary: Prime Day deals on Amazon devices are less attractive than they were before the August price hike. The discounts are still considered worth grabbing.

title: BougeRV DuneRover remote-controlled wagon hauls 200 lb and crosses sand
content:
BougeRV’s remote‑controlled wagon, the DuneRover, has been described as both silly and surprisingly useful. The reviewer received a Kickstarter prototype that features animated lighting and a design intended for hauling heavy gear.

The prototype demonstrated enough torque to flatten hills while carrying over 200 pounds of equipment. It also proved capable of traversing soft sand that typically defeats conventional wagons. The reviewer, who frequently uses various wagons for gear transport, called the DuneRover an epiphany.

Production units are scheduled to ship in February 2027. The Verge published the full review of the prototype.
summary: The DuneRover remote-controlled wagon from BougeRV, shown as a Kickstarter prototype, has enough torque to flatten hills while carrying over 200 pounds of gear. It can also traverse soft sand that defeats conventional wagons, and production units won’t ship until February 2027.
author: The Verge

title: Anthropic says its AI agents did not breach Australian government websites
content:
During a joint parliamentary hearing on artificial intelligence, Anthropic’s head of safeguards, Dave Orr, said that investigations of hundreds of millions of transcripts revealed no unauthorised interactions with Australian government systems.

Orr acknowledged that Anthropic has limited visibility into customer usage because of its standard “zero data retention” policies.

Anthropic also told the AI inquiry that it has never tried to dictate Australian copyright rules.
summary: During a joint parliamentary hearing, Anthropic head of safeguards Dave Orr said investigations of hundreds of millions of transcripts found no unauthorized interactions with Australian government systems. Orr noted Anthropic has limited visibility into customer usage because of its standard zero data retention policies.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Norway plans temporary ban on smart glasses in certain public places
content:
Norway is preparing a temporary ban on smart glasses in a range of public locations. The Oslo government plans to introduce a bill that would prohibit the use of camera‑enabled spectacles in parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres, schools, daycare centres, healthcare facilities, gyms and public events, while still allowing private use.

The move comes as camera‑enabled Meta spectacles have already been restricted in the United Kingdom and the United States over concerns about covert recording. Norway’s proposal reflects growing global apprehension about the spread of AI‑enabled recording devices.
summary: Norway is preparing a temporary ban on camera-enabled smart glasses in locations including parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres, schools, daycare centres, healthcare facilities, gyms and public events, amid rising global concern about AI-enabled recording devices. Private use of the devices would still be permitted.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Pull The Plug plans to disrupt Nvidia executive dinner in London
content:
Protesters affiliated with the anti‑AI movement Pull The Plug are planning direct action against a technology industry event, according to a recent meeting of the group’s cell in a bar below Waterloo Bridge. The cell, which met last week, discussed disrupting a dinner that will be addressed by a senior executive from chip maker Nvidia.

Campaign groups focused on AI safety have reported a surge in membership following a series of AI safety alerts and apocalyptic warnings. Emma, a 28‑year‑old bartender, attended the planning session as one of four plotters from Pull The Plug and said she had never before taken direct action, describing herself as the most nervous participant.
summary: Campaign groups report a surge in membership after AI safety alerts and apocalyptic warnings. A Pull The Plug cell met in a bar below Waterloo Bridge to plot disrupting a tech industry dinner addressed by a senior Nvidia executive, with Emma, a 28‑year‑old bartender, joining the four plotters.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Morning news bulletin for October 6, 2026 covering Europe and global stories
content: On the morning of October 6, 2026, a news bulletin titled “Latest news bulletin” was issued, inviting audiences to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond. The bulletin highlights coverage of the latest and breaking news across World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture and Travel.
summary: The bulletin highlights the most important stories from Europe and beyond on October 6, 2026. It includes coverage of world, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel news.
